To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the age structure of a population is a key determinant of cultural change over generations; (2) the temporal dynamic of change retains a stronger signature for inference than the cultural composition at a specific point of time; (3) in order to infer the individual level processes underlying the observed population level pattern of cultural change, one must first identify the processes that are likely to produce it, and then eliminate the remaining ones.

(i) the patterns observed at group level are rooted in the interaction between the transmission pathways, and the age structure, and (ii) that temporal dynamic of cultural evolution over time retains a signature stronger than the cultural composition at a specific point.

(1) the age structure of a population has a strong influence on the cultural composition of a population, and (2) the cultural composition of populations can be used to infer the relative importance of cultural inheritance mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interface between individual level processes and population level patterns.
understanding how population level patterns in human cultural evolution emerge from individual level processes.
understanding how group level patterns emerge from individual level processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cultural transmission is a complex process, and the patterns observed at population level do not allow us to infer the underlying processes with any certainty.

the population level statistics that are most likely to be informative about transmission processes are the ones that capture the temporal dynamics of the population, such as the rate of cultural change, rather than the composition of the population.
there is no single best way to study cultural evolution, but rather a number of complementary approaches that can be used depending on the question at hand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the population level statistics are a result of a complex interplay of individual level processes, and that the temporal dynamic retains a stronger signature for the transmission pathways than does the composition of the population.
the population level statistics used in the analysis of cultural evolution data are not necessarily a good proxy for the underlying individual level processes.
we have developed a simulation model that allows us to explore the relationship between individual level processes and population level outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the population level patterns observed in human cultural evolution can be explained by a variety of individual level processes.
the population level patterns observed in cultural evolution are not a direct reflection of the individual level processes driving them.

, while it is not possible to identify the specific individual level processes that produced a given pattern in the data, it may be possible to exclude certain individual level processes from the set of plausible explanations.
